transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-30 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Leah Kim (Redwood AE), Marco D'Souza (Redwood SE), Aisha Ng (Citrine CTO), Miguel Torres (ML Eng), Janet Cho (Infra)

Summary:
Quick discovery for Citrine Insights evaluating Redwood's self-serve hosted API vs Dedicated / Private options. Focus on fastest path to first API request with free credits, compliance concerns (SSO, KMS), and pilot benchmarks (latency & cost).

Topics: credits/quickstart, hosting fit (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security controls (SSO, SOC2, KMS), TTFC (time-to-first-call), pilot metrics, next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Leah: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
[00:03] Aisha: yep, loud and clear. thanks for setting this up.
[00:07] Leah: awesome. quick intro from our side — I'm Leah, account exec on the platform team. marco is our solutions engineer, he'll cover infra and benchmarks.
[00:15] Marco: hi all. happy to dive in, esp on pilot setup and what to measure.
[00:19] Aisha: great. from Citrine I'm Aisha, CTO, with miguel who does the ML infra and janet who runs platform. want to figure out how fast we can get to a production-like call with real data and costs.
[00:31] Miguel: yes, especially curious about the free credits path — we don't want to wait on procurement for a POC.
[00:36] Leah: cool, that's exactly what the self-serve credits are for. typical flow is: we hand over a credit code, you spin up an API key in the console, run <1000 requests initially, and we help with a 1:1 with an SE if you need it. most teams are hitting a first meaningful request within a day.
[00:52] Janet: "a day" meaning first successful inference against our data, not just a hello world, right?
[00:57] Marco: yeah, that depends. if you use the hosted API and a curated model, it's literally the SDK, the prompt and then call — could be same-day. for model variants or private onprem, there is infra setup which is longer.
[01:11] Aisha: can you summarize differences between hosted, dedicated and private, like in plain terms?
[01:16] Marco: sure. hosted is our managed API — fastest onboarding, pay-as-you-go with credits, no infra for you. dedicated is reserved GPU pools for single-customer capacity (predictable throughput, lower unit cost at scale), and private is VPC/on-prem for customers needing full control & compliance — there's a customer-managed network and optional air-gapped install.
[01:33] Miguel: any quick numbers on latency vs cost for hosted vs dedicated? ballpark is fine for evaluation.
[01:38] Marco: ballpark yes — hosted for a 2k token context on a modern open model is ~80-150ms per token on our fastest profile, cost slightly higher per token due to multi-tenant overhead. dedicated reduces per-token cost by ~20-40% depending on commit and allows lower tail latency because of pinned instances. private varies a lot by your hardware.
[01:56] Aisha: got it. our use case is customer-facing summarization where tail latency matters under 300ms ideally. we also need SOC2 and SSO.
[02:06] Leah: we have SOC2, SSO/SAML support, RBAC, and KMS integrations. we'll share the security pack after.
[02:11] Janet: can you store model logs but not the raw PII? we have to retain request traces for debugging but keep data residency rules.
[02:18] Marco: yes — audit logs and request-level tracing are optional. you can configure retention and masking. for private installs we can keep everything behind your KMS.
[02:25] Miguel: on the self-serve credits — any limits that would block a meaningful bench? like concurrency or burst caps?
[02:31] Leah: credits usually come with trial quotas. we often bump concurrency for pilots if you ask us. we don't want the out-of-the-box quota to be a blocker.
[02:37] Aisha: how do we instrument cost-per-call quickly?
[02:40] Marco: we give token-level accounting in the console. for the pilot I'll attach a small benchmark script that logs tokens, latency, success rates. you can run it against hosted with the credit and then again against a dedicated config if you decide to trial reserved capacity.
[02:56] Miguel: cool. can you also include guidance on batching and prefix caching? our workload is mostly few-shot summarization where we have a stable prompt template.
[03:05] Marco: absolutely. batching and KV prefix caching are big for throughput and cost. note: automated prefix caching is enabled on certain models; we can show results from similar customers.
[03:15] Aisha: one risk is procurement — we may not get PO signed quickly. can we run a POC entirely on self-serve credits without an enterprise contract?
[03:23] Leah: yes, self-serve can cover that initial evaluation. if you need an SLA or dedicated guarantees later, we convert to a committed plan.
[03:30] Miguel: any gotchas around secrets management? we use a KMS provider and rotate keys frequently.
[03:35] Marco: you can integrate with your KMS — for hosted we offer envelope encryption and you can bring your key for certain enterprise tiers. private gives you full control.
[03:43] Janet: we also run strict network egress rules. would hosted API calls require us to open outbound to multiple regions?
[03:49] Marco: we have region-specific endpoints. if you pick a region we can restrict routing there. dedicated in a cloud region helps too. private is only in your VPC so it meets strict egress rules.
[03:59] Aisha: if we start with hosted credits and then convert to dedicated, how smooth is the migration — do we need code changes?
[04:06] Leah: API is the same across hosted/dedicated/private. routing and model variants can be swapped via config. minimal code changes — mostly config, keys and endpoint updates if you go private.
[04:15] Miguel: nice. now, latency targets: we want p95 under 300ms, p99 as low as possible. any customers with similar SLO?
[04:23] Marco: yes — retail chatbots and summarization customers run at p95 ~150-250ms on dedicated. for p99 we tune batching and instance sizing. we'll share anonymized benchmarks.
[04:33] Aisha: perfect. about models — do you host only open models or also support private fine-tuned models?
[04:39] Marco: we host curated open models and you can bring-your-own models for private deployments. we also support served fine-tunes via model versioning — the private or dedicated lanes are better for customer-owned weights for compliance.
[04:52] (short crosstalk)
[04:55] Speaker 1: mhm mhm
[04:57] Leah: earlier someone asked about sample scripts — I'll drop a small benchmark script that hits the API with a real prompt shape, measures token counts and latency.
[05:06] Miguel: if we run that with our dataset, how quickly can we expect actionable numbers?
[05:11] Marco: within an hour you have raw metrics. you'll want to run a few thousand requests for stable numbers on p95/p99. the credits should cover that.
[05:20] Janet: if we need to run a private pilot on our infra, what's the typical timeline?
[05:25] Marco: private on-prem install is the longest — 4-8 weeks typically depending on air-gap and validation. VPC-managed private is faster, like 1-2 weeks, and dedicated is usually ~1-2 weeks to provision once contract is in place.
[05:39] Aisha: okay. procurement aside, our immediate goal is a hosted quick eval to validate latency and cost impacts using our prompt templates. then we may run a dedicated pilot if numbers make sense.
[05:50] Leah: sounds like a good plan. we'll provide credits and the benchmark script, and Marco can run a short technical call to walk through running the script and interpreting results.
[05:59] Miguel: will you provide sample billing estimates so we can map to unit economics?
[06:04] Leah: yes — we'll send a simple spreadsheet: tokens per call, avg tokens, projected qps, monthly cost at hosted and at dedicated with a few commit levels.
[06:14] Janet: security docs?
[06:16] Leah: I'll attach the SOC2 pack, SAML guide, and KMS integration notes.
[06:21] Aisha: any concerns about vendor lock-in if we start with hosted?
[06:24] Marco: API is consistent and we support exportable model artifacts where possible; plus you can lift and shift to private with minimal code churn.
[06:32] Miguel: what about rate limiting and graceful degradation during spikes? we have unpredictable traffic.
[06:38] Marco: we have soft rate limiting with burst allowances for hosted; dedicated lets you set higher caps. we also have smart routing and fallback policies so you can degrade to a cheaper model variant under load to maintain availability.
[06:50] Aisha: good. let's talk success criteria — what would a successful 2-week hosted pilot look like?
[06:55] Miguel: from our side: 1) p95 under 300ms on production-shaped calls, 2) cost per summary within our target, 3) no unacceptable data leakage in logs.
[07:04] Leah: makes sense. we'll call that out in the pilot doc.
[07:08] Janet: last thing — SSO provisioning. we use SAML and SCIM for user provisioning.
[07:13] Marco: supported; we'll provide steps and a test account flow.
[07:17] (pause)
[07:20] Aisha: ok thanks, this covers most. can we schedule the technical run-through?
[07:24] Marco: yes — I'm available Thurs Apr 7 or Mon Apr 4 — which works?
[07:30] Aisha: Apr 4 works for us in the morning Pacific.
[07:34] Leah: I'll put that on the calendar. I'll also send credits and the quickstart guide right after this call.
[07:41] Miguel: one more thing — do you have an example of request masking for PII?
[07:45] Marco: yes, we have configurable masking presets and regex rules. I'll include examples in the security pack.
[07:52] Aisha: thanks.
[07:54] Leah: great. any other questions?
[07:56] Miguel: none from me.
[07:58] Janet: all good.
[08:00] Leah: wrap up then — recap and next steps.
